<details class="project p-purple" id="mindtheai">
<summary><span class="psummary"><span class="ptitle">MindTheAI (CMD-F 2026)</span><span class="pitch">A Chrome extension for responsible AI use that protects sensitive information, flags unreliable sources and nudges users to rethink unnecessary prompts. Won the 1Password security prize.</span><span class="pmeta"><span class="pcat">Hackathon</span> · Chrome extension · Responsible AI · Security · March 2026</span></span><span class="ptoggle"></span></summary>

::: {.pbody}

[Overview]{.plabel}

MindTheAI is a Chrome extension built at the CMD-F 2026 hackathon to help people use AI tools more thoughtfully and more safely.

[What it does]{.plabel}

- Password protection, so sensitive details stay out of AI prompts
- Removes personal data and prompt filler before a prompt is sent
- Flags unreliable sources
- Usage reminders that nudge users to rethink unnecessary prompts
- Helps users understand the impacts of AI usage

[Result]{.plabel}

Won the **1Password sponsor prize** for the best integration of security practices into a coding project. Winners received $100 and 1Password subscriptions.

[Overview]{.plabel}

A 24-hour hackathon with 200+ participants and 50+ projects. Our coffee-chat conversation starter helps people break the ice: users add a few details in a popup and get useful conversation topics.

[Result]{.plabel}

Winner of the **Social track** and **3rd place overall**. After presenting to 7 judges, we were invited to present to the whole hackathon community of 250+ people. Winners received $200 and had the project featured on the cmd-f website.

A 48-hour [American Statistical Association DataFest](https://ww2.amstat.org/education/datafest/){target="_blank"} competition, completed with a team of 3.

[Approach]{.plabel}

Extensive exploratory data analysis followed by a Bayesian model. Everything was built in Quarto so the full analysis can be reproduced from start to finish.

[Deliverables]{.plabel}

A data dashboard, a demonstration video and presentation slides.

[Overview]{.plabel}

Consulting work for a client in medical research, analyzing changes after glaucoma eye surgery (STAT 450).

[Process]{.plabel}

- Presented regularly to Professor Rodolfo Lourenzutti to keep the work high-quality and reliable
- Met with the client and gave technical oral presentations to the class
- Presented the findings at a poster session
- Produced written reports, a code repository and visualizations in R and GitHub

[What I learned]{.plabel}

Study design, model selection and how to communicate statistics clearly to a non-statistical audience.

<details class="project p-purple" id="research">
<summary><span class="psummary"><span class="ptitle">Weather Extremes Research</span><span class="pitch">Summer research assistantship (NSERC USRA) using time series analysis in Python and R to find patterns in Canadian floods, droughts and wildfires.</span><span class="pmeta"><span class="pcat">Research</span> · Python · R · Time series · EDA · Quarto</span></span><span class="ptoggle"></span></summary>

::: {.pbody}

[Overview]{.plabel}

Research assistant at UBC in summer 2024, funded by an NSERC Undergraduate Student Research Award and supervised by Professors Harry Joe and Natalia Nolde.

[What I did]{.plabel}

I explored Canadian weather data on floods, droughts and wildfires, using exploratory analysis and time series methods to look for patterns. I analyzed research papers, presented my work weekly and used Quarto for presentations.

[Status]{.plabel}

I'm cleaning up the code to publish it in a public repository.

<summary><span class="psummary"><span class="ptitle">wordplayr, an R package</span><span class="pitch">A documented R package with a vignette and a pkgdown website that finds patterns in word lists.</span><span class="pmeta"><span class="pcat">Engineering</span> · R · Roxygen · pkgdown · Vignettes</span></span><span class="ptoggle"></span></summary>

[Overview]{.plabel}

`wordplayr` finds patterns in a list of words: average word length, common starting letters, frequent vowel sounds and more.

[Why I built it]{.plabel}

I've kept a list of my favorite words for years and wanted to understand why I like them. (They most often start with "C".)

[What's included]{.plabel}

A README with install instructions, a vignette, a package website and Roxygen documentation.

[Repository](https://github.com/hlan22/wordplay){target="_blank"} · [Website](https://hlan22.github.io/wordplay/){target="_blank"}
:::

</details>

```{=html}
<script>
function openFromHash() {
  var id = location.hash.slice(1), el = id && document.getElementById(id);
  if (el && el.tagName === "DETAILS") { el.open = true; el.scrollIntoView(); }
}
window.addEventListener("hashchange", openFromHash);
document.addEventListener("DOMContentLoaded", function () {
  openFromHash();
  document.querySelectorAll(".gallery").forEach(function (g) {
    var t = g.querySelector(".gallery-track"), p = g.querySelector(".g-prev"), n = g.querySelector(".g-next");
    if (t.children.length < 2) { p.style.display = n.style.display = "none"; return; }
    p.onclick = function () { t.scrollBy({ left: -t.clientWidth, behavior: "smooth" }); };
    n.onclick = function () { t.scrollBy({ left: t.clientWidth, behavior: "smooth" }); };
  });
});
</script>
```
